info.name: PayFlo API
info.description:
A walkthrough of the PayFlo API in the order a merchant meets it. Run the folders top to bottom: each request stores the ids and credentials the next ones need in collection variables.

The defaults are the development values of the one-command demo (`python demo/demo.py`): the demo merchant's login and the gateway's development admin key. `baseUrl` is the gateway.

The contract is docs/api/openapi.yaml; this collection is the same API as a runnable script.

item.name: 1. Sign up and log in
item.description: Public routes. Login stores the JWT that the rest of the collection sends as a Bearer token.

request.description: An email that is already registered gets the same 201: signup never reveals whether an account exists.
A refresh token works once; this stores the new pair.

item.name: 2. Set up the merchant
item.description: Profile, payout account and (simulated) KYC make the merchant ACTIVE, which settlement requires.

request.description: Owner only, and the password again.
The secret is shown only in this response. It is stored in the collection variables for the requests below.
The target is operations-service's own test receiver. The signing secret is shown only here.

item.name: 3. Take a payment (API key)
item.description: As the merchant's backend: HTTP Basic with the API key from step 2.

header.description: A new key per send. Send the same value twice to see a replay.

request.description: Comes back AUTHORIZING. Try vpa fail@okaxis (rejected) or capturefail@okaxis (capture refused) on a new order.
Send again after a few seconds: the simulated bank moves it to CAPTURED or FAILED.
4000000000000002 is declined, 4000000000000069 is expired, 4000000000000341 has its capture refused.

item.name: 6. Platform operator (admin key)
item.description: X-Admin-Key, never a merchant credential. Set the adminKey variable to the gateway's ADMIN_API_KEY.

item.name: Run a settlement for the merchant

The merchant's next request is 403 MERCHANT_SUSPENDED.
